messages.subject: nominal response model
parts: How could we interpret the parameters of nominal response model "a1, ak0, ak1, ak2, ak3 " what is the difference between the a1 and ak parameters?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: nominal response model
parts: a1 is the overall discrimination for the item, while the ak values are the 'scoring' coefficients, and indicate the category ordering. Try using itemplot(shiny=TRUE) and change the item-class to 'nominal' to get a feel for how they work.

messages.author: 3fd30254cc2deeb1
messages.subject: Re: nominal response model
parts: Thank you so much. I have another question about the "d" parameter.  Do do,d1,d2,d3 parameters show  the difficulty for each category from lowest to highest? Is there also overall difficulty parameter for the item?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: nominal response model
parts:
I wouldn't call them difficulties per say, more like likelihood of being endorsed (larger values indicate that a category was selected often, whereas negative values indicate the category was rarely selected). No there is no overall difficulty value.

Phil

messages.author: 3fd30254cc2deeb1
messages.subject: Re: nominal response model
parts:
I estimated the 3 parameter logistic model and coded it as mod1PL, and estimated the nominal response model and coded as modNOM, then I compared them in terms of overall model fit by the code 
                                            " anova(mod1PL, modNOM)"
and the result is;
     
       AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC                logLik       X2         df   p
1 67910.28 67931.36 68166.58 68547.79      -33835.14      NaN        NaN NaN
2 31385.84 31390.93 31514.03 31704.64      -15632.92 36404.44 9998951365   1

as you see the difference is very big between the dichotomous and polytomous model in terms of log likelihood, I made anova for all dichotomous models and nominal response, and all results show the no significant difference between dichotomous and nominal model. Therefore, I feel that it is not meaningful to compare dichotomous and polytomous models by anova. bUT I am not sure

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: nominal response model
parts:
It is not meaningful to compare any models where the datasets used to fit them are not the same. This is analogous to changing your total sample size by modifying your dependent variable, and therefore these models are in no way nested. 

Phil
